candidates.statement: Gateway checkout returns 502 because the order service returns 502, which traces show originates from the payment service returning 503 on POST /v1/authorizations; the failure is a downstream server error propagated up the chain, not gateway-local.
candidates.uncertainty: Payment-side cause of the 503 (config, saturation, or crash) is not observable in current evidence; only the propagation path is established.

report.explanation: Traces show a consistent chain: gateway /v1/checkout 502 <- order /v1/orders 502 <- payment /v1/authorizations 503, while inventory/reservations succeed. Gateway logs and metrics confirm 502s on /v1/checkout with low latency, so the gateway is propagating a downstream server error. The bounded candidate is an HTTP 5xx fault originating downstream; the payment-side root cause is not yet established.
missing_evidence: Payment service logs/traces explaining why POST /v1/authorizations returns 503
Payment service metrics (error rate, saturation, resource usage) during the incident window
